sections.title: Greeting
sections.line: Paul writes as an apostle by God's will, not his own.

sections.title: Chosen before the foundation
sections.line: Election stated as praise, closing on the first refrain.

sections.title: Redeemed, and let in on the plan
sections.line: Blood-bought forgiveness, then the secret: everything gathered into Christ.

sections.title: Sealed and guaranteed
sections.line: The Spirit as deposit on an inheritance not yet paid.

themes.note: Every blessing is located in him, never merely alongside him.

themes.theme: To the praise of his glory
themes.note: The refrain closing each movement, naming the whole point.
Each gift traced to God's purpose, never to our merit.
Settled before the world began, and repeated to make it stick.

references.why: Israel's own election language — a people treasured and chosen — handed to a largely Gentile church without apology.
Israel was God's portion and inheritance; Paul transfers that status, so Gentile believers inherit rather than merely benefit.
Paul's fuller chain from foreknowledge to glory, so predestination reads here as pastoral assurance rather than abstract decree.
Near-identical wording in the twin letter, showing redemption-as-forgiveness was settled phrasing for Paul, not improvised here.
The same commercial word for a deposit, so the Spirit is a down payment on something already bought.

purpose.statement: Paul wants us to know our standing was settled before the world existed, so that nothing that happens inside it can unsettle it.
He wants us to believe God has disclosed one plan — everything gathered into Christ — because our own salvation only makes sense as part of it.
He wants us to read the Spirit as a deposit rather than a reward, so that assurance rests on what God has paid, not on our progress.
